title: The Last Oath Again
premise: Ada Vane, a mercenary bound by oath to a god who fell silent a century ago, has spent her whole life in the Hollow Valley, the one place magic cannot follow. When a stranger named Corin Ash arrives carrying a prophecy book that names tonight's date and his own death, Ada breaks her one rule and leaves the valley with him. To save him — and the soul he unknowingly sold to the court beneath the mountain before he was born — they must steal it back before the moon completes its thirteenth turn, while the silent god's church hunts them for breaking the valley's peace. In the end Ada discovers her god never went silent but was imprisoned by his own clergy, and she must choose between restoring divine law or forging justice outside it; she frees the god only to refuse him, keeping her oath to Corin instead.
about_author: Zephyrine Galloway is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval oath-books before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about broken promises, stubborn mercenaries, and gods who overstay their welcome.

chapters.title: The Valley Where Magic Cannot Follow
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She takes a routine escort job through the Hollow Valley, establishing its eerie magiclessness and her mercenary code. A quiet chapter of competence and loneliness; the emotional beat is the ache of belonging nowhere, even in the place that raised her.

chapters.title: A Stranger With Tomorrow's Date
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Corin Ash stumbles into a border tavern clutching a century-old prophecy book open to a page bearing tonight's date and his name beside the word 'dead'. Ada saves him from a mob convinced he's an omen. Beat: reluctant curiosity overriding her instinct to walk away.

chapters.title: The Oath That Went Silent
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, with flashback. We learn of her childhood swearing to the god Vessel-Who-Waits and the day his voice stopped. The church elders order her to surrender Corin as heretical cargo. Beat: the first crack between duty and conscience.

chapters.title: Thirteen Turns
chapters.summary: Corin's POV. Reading further into the prophecy book, he learns his soul was sold to the court beneath the mountain generations ago, payable when the moon completes its thirteenth turn — twelve nights away. Beat: terror transmuting into grim resolve.

chapters.title: Leaving the Hollow
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Crossing the valley border, Ada feels magic flood back — including the faint, wrong pulse of her dead god's oath-mark burning on her wrist. Church hunters follow. Beat: exhilaration shadowed by guilt at abandoning everything she swore to protect.

chapters.title: The Road Sells Its Secrets
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. On the road they trade histories: Corin's merchant family's old debt, Ada's years of contracts. A church ambush forces their first fight together. Beat: trust built in blood, awkward and real.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. They reach the mountain city of Karsthold, where the soul-court holds market under torchlight: memories, names, and years traded like coin. Beat: wonder curdling into horror at what power does when it becomes currency.

chapters.title: A Debt With His Face
chapters.summary: Corin's POV. In the court archives Corin finds the original contract — signed by his great-grandfather, witnessed by a priest of the Vessel-Who-Waits. The church didn't just know; it brokered the sale. Beat: betrayal reframing everything Ada believed.

chapters.title: What the Moon Owes
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Consulting a disgraced court-scribe, Neme, they learn souls can be reclaimed only by substitution: something of equal weight freely given. Beat: dawning dread as Ada realizes what 'freely given' might cost her.

chapters.title: The Priest Who Brokers Souls
chapters.summary: Neme's POV. High Cleric Ostrevan, keeper of the silent god's rites, offers Ada absolution and Corin's safe passage home — if she delivers the prophecy book and lets the debt stand. Beat: temptation dressed as mercy.

chapters.title: Nine Nights Left
chapters.summary: Corin's POV. Hiding in Karsthold's undercity, Corin begins secretly negotiating to sell his remaining years to buy time, hiding it from Ada. Beat: love expressed as self-destruction; the corruption of power begins small.

chapters.title: The Weight of a Name
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada discovers Corin's secret bargain and they fight bitterly. Neme reveals a loophole: the contract's witness-seal is forged — the god himself never consented. Beat: fury giving way to a fragile new plan.

chapters.title: Breaking Into the Ledger-Hall
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Heist chapter: the trio infiltrates the court's ledger-hall to steal the original contract. They succeed partially — but trigger a soul-writ on Corin's head. Beat: triumph undercut by the alarm bells of consequence.

chapters.title: Hunted Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Fleeing through Karsthold's deep galleries, Neme is captured buying them time. The moon wanes toward its thirteenth turn. Beat: grief and the hardening of Ada's resolve from mercenary pragmatism into something like conviction.

chapters.title: Ostrevan's Confession
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Captured by the church, Ada faces Ostrevan, who confesses: the clergy imprisoned the Vessel-Who-Waits a century ago because his justice threatened their power. Her silence-broken god has been screaming ever since. Beat: shattering revelation — the corruption was institutional all along.

chapters.title: The God Who Was Screaming
chapters.summary: Corin's POV. Rescuing Ada, Corin touches her oath-mark and hears the god directly: he asks not for worship but for release. The moon turns thirteenth at midnight tomorrow. Beat: awe and terrible responsibility.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada refuses Ostrevan's final bargain — Corin's soul for the god's continued imprisonment — and instead rallies Karsthold's debtors, whose stolen souls give the court its power, to rise. Beat: the theme made flesh; power returned to those it was taken from.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Turn
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating POVs. At the moment of collection, Ada offers her own oath-bound life as substitution, voiding the forged seal; the debtors' uprising storms the ledger-hall; Ostrevan falls to the court he fed. Beat: sacrifice, chaos, and the moon completing its turn.

chapters.title: Before the Silent Throne
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. In the god's prison beneath the mountain, Ada stands before the Vessel-Who-Waits, who offers to restore her oath, her purpose, her belonging. Beat: the quietest, hardest choice in the book.

chapters.title: An Oath Kept Is Not an Oath Owned
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada refuses him — keeping her promise to Corin and to herself rather than to any throne — and walks out of the prison as it crumbles, the god freed to wander unowned. Beat: liberation through refusal.

chapters.title: Souls Returned
chapters.summary: Corin's POV. The court dissolves; stolen souls return to their owners across the valley lands, including Neme, alive and changed. Corin, whole, chooses to stay near Ada rather than return to his old life. Beat: restitution and tender, earned intimacy.

chapters.title: The Last Oath Again
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, epilogue. Back in the Hollow Valley — where magic now gently follows — Ada swears a new oath, unwitnessed by any god: to Corin, to Neme, to no master. Beat: belonging chosen, not granted; the story closes on a promise kept by human hands alone.
